Investigative Reporting . Public Interest . Accountability Journalism
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results

An Investigative Journalist uncovers hidden wrongdoing — corruption, fraud, abuse of power — through deep research,
document analysis and source-building, publishing evidence-based stories that hold powerful institutions accountable.
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
Review new documents obtained via RTI request
Call a source to verify a key claim
Cross-check financial records against public filings
Draft a section of the investigative report
Legal review meeting on a sensitive claim
Follow up on a new lead from a reader tip
✓ Strong instinct for uncovering hidden truths
✓ Enjoy deep, methodical research and fact-checking
✓ Comfortable pursuing sensitive or risky stories
✓ Motivated by accountability and public interest impact
✓ Resilient to pressure, pushback and legal scrutiny

• Identify leads and verify tips from sources
  • Request and analyse documents (RTI, court records, filings)
  • Build and protect relationships with confidential sources
  • Cross-check facts across multiple independent sources
  • Write and structure long-form investigative reports
  • Navigate legal review before publication

Every claim must be independently verified with evidence before
publishing.
It's the same as regular news reporting, just slower.
It requires specialised research, legal and source-protection skills.
Anyone can do this with enough persistence.

Rigorous fact-checking, legal literacy and source protocol take
years to master.

Why This Career Appeared In Your Results

A Data Journalist finds and tells stories using data — analysing large datasets, government records and public information,
then visualising findings clearly to reveal patterns and truths words alone cannot show.
Election data desks (news channels) Real-time election data analysis and visualisation
COVID-19 data tracking dashboards Public health data journalism during the pandemic
Indian data-driven policy and economy reporting
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
Clean and structure a newly obtained government dataset
Run statistical analysis to find patterns
Sketch visualisation concepts for key findings
Build charts/maps in a visualisation tool
Fact-check data sources with the editor
✓ Enjoy finding stories hidden inside large datasets
✓ Strong analytical and statistical thinking
✓ Comfortable with coding, spreadsheets and visualisation tools
✓ Interested in blending journalism with technology
✓ Motivated by making complex data understandable

• Source and clean large public or leaked datasets
  • Analyse data using spreadsheets, SQL or Python
  • Identify statistically significant patterns or anomalies
  • Design clear, accurate data visualisations
  • Write the narrative explaining the data's significance
  • Fact-check data sources and methodology
Data journalism is just making charts.
It requires statistical rigor, coding skill and narrative judgment.
You need a computer science degree to do this.

Many data journalists are self-taught through practice and online
courses.
Data speaks for itself without a story.

Raw data needs careful narrative framing to be meaningful to
readers.

accuracy and sourcing · Visual design sense for clear charts

accessible to readers · Working with cutting-edge visualisation

Requires continuous learning of new tools and techniques ·

skills are essential · Simple narratives — data stories require

Science Communication . Research Reporting . Public Understanding
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results

A Science Journalist reports on scientific research, discoveries and policy — reading academic papers, interviewing
researchers and translating complex findings into accurate, engaging stories for a general audience.
The Wire Science / Down To Earth
Public health science communication at scale
Space science reporting for Indian audiences
YouTube science journalism channels Video-based science explainer journalism
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
Read a newly published research paper on a topic
Interview the lead researcher for context
Write the story in accessible, accurate language
Editor review for scientific accuracy and clarity
Track ongoing coverage of a developing science story
✓ Deep curiosity about science and research
✓ Enjoy translating complex ideas into accessible language
✓ Comfortable reading and interpreting academic papers
✓ Interested in the intersection of science, policy and society
✓ Motivated by combating misinformation with accurate reporting

• Read and interpret peer-reviewed research papers
  • Interview scientists and research institutions
  • Fact-check claims against scientific consensus
  • Write clear, accurate stories for general readers
  • Cover science policy and funding developments
  • Correct or contextualise scientific misinformation
Science journalism is just simplifying jargon.

It requires deep comprehension of methodology and statistical
significance.
You need a science PhD to report on science.

Strong research literacy and expert interviewing can be learned
without a doctorate.
All published research findings are equally solid.

Distinguishing preliminary from well-established findings is a core
skill.

Tech Reporting . Product Analysis . Industry Coverage
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results

A Technology Journalist reports on tech products, companies, startups and industry trends — reviewing gadgets, covering
major launches and analysing the business and policy implications of the technology sector.

What Is A Political / Policy Reporter?

A Political or Policy Reporter covers government, elections, legislation and public institutions — explaining how policy
decisions are made and their real-world impact, while navigating a politically sensitive beat with fairness and rigor.

✓ Motivated by informing citizens on issues that affect them
✓ Resilient to scrutiny and politically charged criticism

Political reporters just repeat party talking points.

This beat is only about elections.

round.

statements.

Conflict Reporting . Frontline Journalism . International Affairs
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
What Is A War / Conflict Correspondent?

A War or Conflict Correspondent reports from active conflict zones and crisis regions — documenting events, human impact
and geopolitical context under extreme risk, often for international wire services or major broadcasters.
Reuters/AP/AFP wire correspondents Global conflict-zone news reporting
Freelance conflict photojournalists Independent frontline visual reporting
NDTV/India Today international desks Indian outlets covering global conflicts
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
Security briefing and risk assessment for the day
Travel to a reporting location with a fixer/security team
File the story under a tight deadline
Debrief on safety and plan the next day's coverage
✓ Deep commitment to bearing witness to conflict and crisis
✓ Comfortable with extreme physical and psychological risk
✓ Strong crisis judgment and situational awareness
✓ Motivated by giving voice to affected populations
✓ Resilient under extraordinary pressure and danger

• Assess security risk before entering an area
  • Interview civilians, combatants and officials
  • Verify information amid chaotic, unreliable conditions
  • File reports under extreme time and safety pressure
  • Coordinate with fixers, translators and security teams
  • Process the psychological toll of covering trauma
Most are highly trained in risk assessment and disciplined caution.

It involves trauma exposure, extreme danger and long family
separation.
Anyone brave enough can do this job.

It requires specialised hostile-environment training and
institutional support.

Environmental Reporting . Climate Coverage . Policy Analysis

An Environmental Journalist reports on climate change, pollution, conservation and environmental policy — translating
scientific data and legal complexity into stories that inform the public on ecological issues and accountability.

Independent Journalism . Media Entrepreneurship . Reader-Funded News
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
What Is An Independent Media Founder / Newsletter Creator?

An Independent Media Founder builds and runs their own journalism operation — reporting, writing and publishing directly to
readers via newsletters or websites, and building sustainable revenue through subscriptions rather than a traditional employer.
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
Research and report on a story for the next issue
Pursue a grant application or sponsor conversation
Publish and promote the piece across channels
✓ Strong independent journalistic voice and integrity
✓ Entrepreneurial mindset combined with reporting skill
